Death of a Diplomat: Unanswered Questions in Paris

By: Nickolaus Bauer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africa’s ambassador dies in Paris, leaving more questions than answers - Did Nathi Mthethwa fall — or was he pushed? In the City of Light, a diplomat’s death casts a long shadow

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche will be the only South African media house with local expertise on the ground

Summary:
Main Hook
On the night of 28 September, South Africa’s ambassador to France, Nathi Mthethwa, fell to his death from a room at Paris’s Hyatt Regency.
Was it a tragic accident, suicide, or something more sinister? French prosecutors remain silent, fuelling speculation.
The timing is striking: just days earlier, Mthethwa’s name resurfaced in South Africa at the Madlanga Commission into corruption at the South African Police Service. He was accused of political interference during his tenure as police commissioner — a reminder of the controversies that followed him into his diplomatic career.
Carte Blanche travels to the French capital to piece together the ambassador’s final days — from his joyous interactions at a memorial in Longheuval, to the window from which he plunged, to the unanswered calls for clarity from grieving families and colleagues.
This is not only the story of one man’s untimely death, but also of how France’s justice system handles sensitive investigations in the glare of international scrutiny.


Extra Budget Items:
- Single return flight from Madrid to Paris
- One night's accommodation in the Hyatt Regency
- Travel by cab to various locations in Paris

Press Release:


Death of a Diplomat
What really happened to Ambassador Nathi Mthethwa? The former police minister was found dead outside the Hyatt Regency in Paris last week: he had apparently fallen to his death from a room on the 22nd floor. In the wake of allegations by KwaZulu Natal Police Commissioner Lt Gen Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi at the Madlanga Commission, his sudden death caused a ripple of shock and wild speculation. Carte Blanche retraces Mthethwa’s final days in Paris, and asks: was this suicide? Tragic accident? Or is something more sinister at play?
Producer & Presenter: Nickolaus Bauer

Script:


(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
The death of a diplomat…
(SABC NEWS UPSOUND)
French authorities are investigating the death of South Africa’s ambassador to France: Nathi Mthethwa
(RAFAEL MIRO)
I was there 2 or 3 hours after the news came out that the ambassador had died.
(ENCA UPSOUND)
Its alleged that he fell from the 22nd floor.
(NICHOLAS PAGANELLI)
You can imagine that the life of an ambassador is more important in terms of political consequence than the life of the average citizen
(NEWZROOM UPSOUND)
The courtyard is still sealed by police. Even the hotel staff are not permitted to go there.
(RAFAEL MIRO)
it seemed like nobody paid attention to the death of such an important figure
(SABC NEWS UPSOUND)
Many questions are still being asked about what exactly happened?
(NEWZROOM UPSOUND)
The family says at no point did Nathi Mthethwa ever share any kind of personal crisis or mental anguish with any of them
(DR SFISIO BUTHELEZI)
Boom… On Tuesday he was gone. It adds to the mystery of life.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
On the night of 28 September, South Africa’s ambassador to France, Nathi Mthethwa, fell from a window at this Paris hotel. His sudden death raising troubling questions.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Mthethwa was appointed South Africa’s ambassador to France in early 2024 and it seemed like he was relishing the posting to this G7 nation. Presenting his credentials to officials in Monaco just weeks ago and in his final days joyously dancing with South Africans at a Heritage day event.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
But less than 100 hours later… He was dead.


(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
As out of character as that may have seemed - it is inescapable that days before Mthethwa was named and shamed at the Madlanaga commission of inquiry into political interference and corrutpion at the South African police service - a ministry Mthethwa led for several years.
UPSOUNDS
(NHLANHLA MKHWANAZI)
"He simply says stop prosecuting Mdluli and you must stop disciplinary against Mdluli. Now if you talk about political interference that's the worst I've ever experienced."
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Just hours after Mthethwa’s body was found in the courtyard of the hotel Rafael Miro was one of the first journalists on the scene. Arriving while authorities were still at the hotel and just before a statement was released by French authorities pointing to a suicide.
(RAFAEL MIRO)
I was struck by the general indifference toward the incident. The people there did not know that someone had died less alone. The South African ambassador. And there was only one firefighter, car in the scene. There was no more police cars. And it was as if some nothing had happened.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Some people are characterising the news from the prosecutor's office that early in the investigation to be quite weird.
(RAFAEL MIRO)
There was a lot of information that came out very soon in the investigation. There was a lot of details about, you know, the scissors used to break the window. The letter that he sent to his wife. And I felt like the French prosecutor's office tries to give a lot of details to explain and to prove that it was a suicide.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
The investigation has revealed that one of Mthethwa’s phones was found here in this park - Bois de Bologne. One of Paris’ many picturesque gardens that draws locals and visitors hoping to enjoy some natural beauty during the day. At night though Parisians advise to stay away, as it turns dodgy as soon as the sun goes down. Just under a kilometer from where Mthethwa’s body was found, how and why did his phone end up here?

(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
French police have since come out to refute the claims of Mthethwa’s phone being discovered in the park. But there are many other puzzling aspects to the former minister’s untimely demise. It is understood he booked his room in the hotel weeks before. And then changed the date of his booking - twice.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Guests and staff at the hotel remain tight lipped about the circumstances of the ambassador’s death. Nobody wants to talk to the media. And authorities too have gone to ground after the a statement suggesting it was a suicide.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Ambassador Mthethwa fell to his death from a room exactly like this one. According to hotel staff and investigators, it remained completely untouched, except for the window from which the ambassador fell. It was forced open. Exactly how remains unclear, but according to the investigation, a pair of scissors was found at the scene. But it's hard to imagine how a simple pair of scissors could have been used to force open a window with a security mechanism quite like this one.

(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
South African police have joined the French investigation. But are too offering no comment on their work.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
In search of answers, I turned to Advocate Nicholas Paganelli with over 15 years of experience on the French bar specialising in criminal investigations.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
How does the French judicial system work with regards to a prosecutor a magistrate and indeed a police investigation?
(NICHOLAS PAGANELLI)
In reality, things are quite simple. You have a public prosecutor, in this case the Paris public prosecutor, who leads the investigations and gives instructions to the judicial police officers.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Is there anything about this investigation or indeed this death that puzzles you?
(NICHOLAS PAGANELLI)
For the moment, according to the official statement from the prosecutor's office, there is no evidence to suggest murder. What I find strange is why he's staying in a hotel a few hundred meters from his home? That's curious.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
The South African Embassy in Paris is trying to celebrate the memory of an ambassador that was seemingly loved by his staff and the South African community in the French capital.
Many shuffling in to sign the condolence book. Shellshocked that someone so full of life is dead. Let alone could have killed himself.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Vera Dickman was one of them. A Parisian resident since the 1980s she says Mthethwa’s affable manner energised the South African community. Who loved having an engaged and open ambassador serving as their link to back home.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
In all of the time you did interact with him, did he come across as someone who could be down in the dumps?
(VERA DICKMAN)
He always came across as warm and jovial. And so it's very hard to say. We couldn't tell if he was down in the dumps. This is no way community can see that. I don't, think so. And especially at the last Heritage Day event. When he was dancing and with the others and seemed so happy. No, there was no way of saying he was down in the dumps.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
What do you think this is going to do to the South African community?
(VERA DICKMAN)
The South African community is in shock. People have tried to express their condolences and be close to the family as wella as the folks in the embassy. I know staff enjoyed working with him too. I think people were really caught by surprise.

(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Mthethwa is survived by his wife Philisiwe Buthelezi. Who has been in mourning at the official South African residence since her husband’s death. Joined from South Africa by her brother soon after - Dr Sfiso Buthelezi - the former deputy minister of finance.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Dr Buthelezi, our absolute condolences. Absolute condolences. How is the family holding up this horrific news?
(DR SFISO BUTHLEZI)
Very difficult. Heartbroken. Little bit of confusion, but at the end of the day. I would say we are meeting the challenge.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Do you think that this is in any way connected to him being named at the Madlanga commission of inquiry?
(DR SFISO BUTHLEZI)
There is nothing they would have asked them to do to be able to answer. If was he was always to assist the justice system because he believed in it. He is the former Minister of Police. He has faced far more challenging things in his life.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Is the family worried at all that the French police have got it wrong? The early indications are that this is pointing to a suicide
(DR SFISO BUTHLEZI)
It's still too early for us to say that. That’s why we want to allow the investigators, the police to to their work and we will take it from there.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Did he show any indication whatsoever that he was stressed, that he was upset?
(DR SFISO BUTHLEZI)
He was a friend, he was a brother. We spoke up about many things. There was never a time in which he indicated he was having something in which matt lead him to - if people say that what it is - there was nothing.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
Supporting the suicide claim is an alleged message Mthethwa sent to his wife, apologising and saying he planned to end his life — though it hasn’t been made public. And the family would not comment on that. CCTV footage from the hotel also remains unseen, after being seized by police.
(NICKOLAUS BAUER)
As investigators pieced together Nathi Mthethwa’s final moments. We simply don't know what happened. What was running through his mind in the days before his death. What could have led him to jump? Or was he pushed?

PROMO 1
UPSOUND
VO: Days after being named and shamed at the Madlanga commission of enquiry, the former minister of police winds up dead.
UPSOUND (DR SFISO BUTHELEZI) We didn’t have any indication that he was even going to be called.
VO: Suspicion abounds as puzzling details of Nathi Mthethwa’s death continue to emerge.
UPSOUND (RAFAEL MIRO) The morning after the incident, there was already no one else talking about it. It was as if it was an incident that happened outside of France. But it happened like in the centre of Paris.


PROMO 2
VO: Accident – suicide – or something more sinister?
UPSOUND (SFISO BUTHELEZI) Anything and everything is assist us to be to understand and to demystify the mystery we aretalking about is much welcomed.
VO: French and South African police look for answers to the death of Nathi Mthetwha
UPSOUND (NICOLAS PAGANELLI) The French police will have to deliver results because this is a very important person. And they will also have to communicate with the South African authorities

PROMO 3
VO: Days after being accused of political interference, Nathi Mthethwa plunged to his death in Paris. Was it really suicide?
UPSOUND: (VERA DICKMAN) We couldn’t tell if he was down in the dumps.
VO: We piece together his final days, and the questions that remain unanswered.
UPSOUND: (NICOLAS PAGANELLI) No one has the right to know what is in an investigation file, unless the prosecutor decides to make an official statement.

J, XRC021 Ominous Steps Mood 19 00:00:45 Deaner Volante Blinq175 TX Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 12 October 2025 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 13 October 2025 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: Death of a Diplomat What really happened to Ambassador Nathi Mthethwa? The former police minister was found dead outside the Hyatt Regency in Paris last week: he had apparently fallen to his death from a room on the 22nd floor. In the wake of allegations by KwaZulu Natal Police Commissioner Lt Gen Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi at the Madlanga Commission, his sudden death caused a ripple of shock and wild speculation. Carte Blanche retraces Mthethwa’s final days in Paris, and asks: was this suicide? Tragic accident? Or is something more sinister at play? Producer & Presenter: Nickolaus Bauer Script: (NICKOLAUS BAUER) The death of a diplomat… (SABC NEWS UPSOUND) French authorities are investigating the death of South Africa’s ambassador to France: Nathi Mthethwa (RAFAEL MIRO) I was there 2 or 3 hours after the news came out that the ambassador had died. (ENCA UPSOUND) Its alleged that he fell from the 22nd floor. (NICHOLAS PAGANELLI) You can imagine that the life of an ambassador is more important in terms of political consequence than the life of the average citizen (NEWZROOM UPSOUND) The courtyard is still sealed by police. Even the hotel staff are not permitted to go there. (RAFAEL MIRO) it seemed like nobody paid attention to the death of such an important figure (SABC NEWS UPSOUND) Many questions are still being asked about what exactly happened? (NEWZROOM UPSOUND) The family says at no point did Nathi Mthethwa ever share any kind of personal crisis or mental anguish with any of them (DR SFISIO BUTHELEZI) Boom… On Tuesday he was gone. It adds to the mystery of life. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) On the night of 28 September, South Africa’s ambassador to France, Nathi Mthethwa, fell from a window at this Paris hotel. His sudden death raising troubling questions. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Mthethwa was appointed South Africa’s ambassador to France in early 2024 and it seemed like he was relishing the posting to this G7 nation. Presenting his credentials to officials in Monaco just weeks ago and in his final days joyously dancing with South Africans at a Heritage day event. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) But less than 100 hours later… He was dead. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) As out of character as that may have seemed - it is inescapable that days before Mthethwa was named and shamed at the Madlanaga commission of inquiry into political interference and corrutpion at the South African police service - a ministry Mthethwa led for several years. UPSOUNDS (NHLANHLA MKHWANAZI) "He simply says stop prosecuting Mdluli and you must stop disciplinary against Mdluli. Now if you talk about political interference that's the worst I've ever experienced." (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Just hours after Mthethwa’s body was found in the courtyard of the hotel Rafael Miro was one of the first journalists on the scene. Arriving while authorities were still at the hotel and just before a statement was released by French authorities pointing to a suicide. (RAFAEL MIRO) I was struck by the general indifference toward the incident. The people there did not know that someone had died less alone. The South African ambassador. And there was only one firefighter, car in the scene. There was no more police cars. And it was as if some nothing had happened. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Some people are characterising the news from the prosecutor's office that early in the investigation to be quite weird. (RAFAEL MIRO) There was a lot of information that came out very soon in the investigation. There was a lot of details about, you know, the scissors used to break the window. The letter that he sent to his wife. And I felt like the French prosecutor's office tries to give a lot of details to explain and to prove that it was a suicide. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) The investigation has revealed that one of Mthethwa’s phones was found here in this park - Bois de Bologne. One of Paris’ many picturesque gardens that draws locals and visitors hoping to enjoy some natural beauty during the day. At night though Parisians advise to stay away, as it turns dodgy as soon as the sun goes down. Just under a kilometer from where Mthethwa’s body was found, how and why did his phone end up here? (NICKOLAUS BAUER) French police have since come out to refute the claims of Mthethwa’s phone being discovered in the park. But there are many other puzzling aspects to the former minister’s untimely demise. It is understood he booked his room in the hotel weeks before. And then changed the date of his booking - twice. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Guests and staff at the hotel remain tight lipped about the circumstances of the ambassador’s death. Nobody wants to talk to the media. And authorities too have gone to ground after the a statement suggesting it was a suicide. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Ambassador Mthethwa fell to his death from a room exactly like this one. According to hotel staff and investigators, it remained completely untouched, except for the window from which the ambassador fell. It was forced open. Exactly how remains unclear, but according to the investigation, a pair of scissors was found at the scene. But it's hard to imagine how a simple pair of scissors could have been used to force open a window with a security mechanism quite like this one. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) South African police have joined the French investigation. But are too offering no comment on their work. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) In search of answers, I turned to Advocate Nicholas Paganelli with over 15 years of experience on the French bar specialising in criminal investigations. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) How does the French judicial system work with regards to a prosecutor a magistrate and indeed a police investigation? (NICHOLAS PAGANELLI) In reality, things are quite simple. You have a public prosecutor, in this case the Paris public prosecutor, who leads the investigations and gives instructions to the judicial police officers. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Is there anything about this investigation or indeed this death that puzzles you? (NICHOLAS PAGANELLI) For the moment, according to the official statement from the prosecutor's office, there is no evidence to suggest murder. What I find strange is why he's staying in a hotel a few hundred meters from his home? That's curious. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) The South African Embassy in Paris is trying to celebrate the memory of an ambassador that was seemingly loved by his staff and the South African community in the French capital. Many shuffling in to sign the condolence book. Shellshocked that someone so full of life is dead. Let alone could have killed himself. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Vera Dickman was one of them. A Parisian resident since the 1980s she says Mthethwa’s affable manner energised the South African community. Who loved having an engaged and open ambassador serving as their link to back home. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) In all of the time you did interact with him, did he come across as someone who could be down in the dumps? (VERA DICKMAN) He always came across as warm and jovial. And so it's very hard to say. We couldn't tell if he was down in the dumps. This is no way community can see that. I don't, think so. And especially at the last Heritage Day event. When he was dancing and with the others and seemed so happy. No, there was no way of saying he was down in the dumps. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) What do you think this is going to do to the South African community? (VERA DICKMAN) The South African community is in shock. People have tried to express their condolences and be close to the family as wella as the folks in the embassy. I know staff enjoyed working with him too. I think people were really caught by surprise. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Mthethwa is survived by his wife Philisiwe Buthelezi. Who has been in mourning at the official South African residence since her husband’s death. Joined from South Africa by her brother soon after - Dr Sfiso Buthelezi - the former deputy minister of finance. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Dr Buthelezi, our absolute condolences. Absolute condolences. How is the family holding up this horrific news? (DR SFISO BUTHLEZI) Very difficult. Heartbroken. Little bit of confusion, but at the end of the day. I would say we are meeting the challenge. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Do you think that this is in any way connected to him being named at the Madlanga commission of inquiry? (DR SFISO BUTHLEZI) There is nothing they would have asked them to do to be able to answer. If was he was always to assist the justice system because he believed in it. He is the former Minister of Police. He has faced far more challenging things in his life. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Is the family worried at all that the French police have got it wrong? The early indications are that this is pointing to a suicide (DR SFISO BUTHLEZI) It's still too early for us to say that. That’s why we want to allow the investigators, the police to to their work and we will take it from there. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Did he show any indication whatsoever that he was stressed, that he was upset? (DR SFISO BUTHLEZI) He was a friend, he was a brother. We spoke up about many things. There was never a time in which he indicated he was having something in which matt lead him to - if people say that what it is - there was nothing. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) Supporting the suicide claim is an alleged message Mthethwa sent to his wife, apologising and saying he planned to end his life — though it hasn’t been made public. And the family would not comment on that. CCTV footage from the hotel also remains unseen, after being seized by police. (NICKOLAUS BAUER) As investigators pieced together Nathi Mthethwa’s final moments. We simply don't know what happened. What was running through his mind in the days before his death. What could have led him to jump? Or was he pushed? PROMO 1 UPSOUND VO: Days after being named and shamed at the Madlanga commission of enquiry, the former minister of police winds up dead. UPSOUND (DR SFISO BUTHELEZI) We didn’t have any indication that he was even going to be called. VO: Suspicion abounds as puzzling details of Nathi Mthethwa’s death continue to emerge. UPSOUND (RAFAEL MIRO) The morning after the incident, there was already no one else talking about it. It was as if it was an incident that happened outside of France. But it happened like in the centre of Paris. PROMO 2 VO: Accident – suicide – or something more sinister? UPSOUND (SFISO BUTHELEZI) Anything and everything is assist us to be to understand and to demystify the mystery we aretalking about is much welcomed. VO: French and South African police look for answers to the death of Nathi Mthetwha UPSOUND (NICOLAS PAGANELLI) The French police will have to deliver results because this is a very important person. And they will also have to communicate with the South African authorities PROMO 3 VO: Days after being accused of political interference, Nathi Mthethwa plunged to his death in Paris. Was it really suicide? UPSOUND: (VERA DICKMAN) We couldn’t tell if he was down in the dumps. VO: We piece together his final days, and the questions that remain unanswered. UPSOUND: (NICOLAS PAGANELLI) No one has the right to know what is in an investigation file, unless the prosecutor decides to make an official statement.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): South Africa’s ambassador dies in Paris, leaving more questions than answers - Did Nathi Mthethwa fall — or was he pushed? In the City of Light, a diplomat’s death casts a long shadow
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche will be the only South African media house with local expertise on the ground
metadata.Summary: Main Hook On the night of 28 September, South Africa’s ambassador to France, Nathi Mthethwa, fell to his death from a room at Paris’s Hyatt Regency. Was it a tragic accident, suicide, or something more sinister? French prosecutors remain silent, fuelling speculation. The timing is striking: just days earlier, Mthethwa’s name resurfaced in South Africa at the Madlanga Commission into corruption at the South African Police Service. He was accused of political interference during his tenure as police commissioner — a reminder of the controversies that followed him into his diplomatic career. Carte Blanche travels to the French capital to piece together the ambassador’s final days — from his joyous interactions at a memorial in Longheuval, to the window from which he plunged, to the unanswered calls for clarity from grieving families and colleagues. This is not only the story of one man’s untimely death, but also of how France’s justice system handles sensitive investigations in the glare of international scrutiny.
